newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine news photographer found murdered.
newsitem.headline: Argentine news photographer found murdered.

text.p: Argentine police said on Sunday they had found the burned body of a magazine photographer, with a gunshot wound in his head and his hands handcuffed behind his back, in his car on a dirt road near the beach resort of Pinamar, southeast of Buenos Aires.

"It was obviously the work of professionals", said local police Chief Inspector Guillermo Lima. He said there were no clues yet as to the motives for the killing of Jose Luis Cabezas, a photographer for Argentina's top-selling weekly news magazine Noticias.

The body of the 35-year-old journalist, who was covering the holiday season in Pinamar, a favourite summer resort for Argentine politicians, was found early on Saturday. It was so badly burned that Cabezas could only be identified by his watch, car keys and dental records.

Local television journalist Guillermo Pereira, one of the first reporters at the scene, said Cabezas "had his head on the driver's seat, his legs on the passenger's seat ... He was totally burned and all you could see were his bones."

The governor of Buenos Aires Province, Eduardo Duhalde, offered a reward for information about the killing, and President Carlos Menem ordered Interior Minister Carlos Corach to make the investigation a top priority.
The circumstances of the killing brought back memories for many people of the murders of Argentine journalists during the 1976-83 military regime.

"If this is a vendetta for some picture he took, it's a signal that should trigger all the red lights and reactivate the memory of a society that has such a dark recent history," the head of the opposition Radical Party, Rodolfo Terragno, told Argentine radio.

The independent journalists' rights group PERIODISTAS called it "a very serious episode that reminds us of similar incidents not so long ago in Argentina's history." The news photographers' association ARGRA said it "should be analysed in the framework of a long list of attacks on our profession."
